subject.title: fix(msteams): reset sessions on app removal lifecycle

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose resetSessionEntryLifecycle as a public Plugin SDK operation with owner-coordinated harness release, or should this Teams fix use a narrower internal lifecycle seam?
rationale: The implementation appears technically coherent and well tested, but choosing the permanent public plugin contract, ownership boundary, and rollback semantics is an architecture decision that automation cannot safely make.

options.title: Sponsor the generic SDK contract
options.body: Accept the documented atomic reset and owner-handoff semantics as the supported plugin API, resolve the final exact-head check, and land the PR.

options.title: Narrow the lifecycle seam
options.body: Keep the Teams behavior but move session rotation behind an internal owner-mediated helper so third-party plugins do not receive a new general session-reset API.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the generic SDK contract
recommendation.body: Accept the documented atomic reset and owner-handoff semantics as the supported plugin API, resolve the final exact-head check, and land the PR.

likelyOwner.reason: They directly shaped the Teams scope on this branch and are the strongest available routing signal for both the channel behavior and permanent SDK boundary decision.
